title: A cells benchmark compares nail's cell fraction on original, reversed and shuffled TrEMBL
body:
## What exists today

pid carries a cells figure that answers a question other than recall against identity. `pid parse cells` reads one nail run's table into `cells.true.tbl` and `cells.decoy.tbl`, nail's cell fraction against query length × target length, and `scripts/plot_cell_frac.py` overlays them as two log-density heatmaps.

## The change

A benchmark of its own, `cells`, for how much of the dynamic-programming matrix nail's cloud search fills depending on whether the target carries signal. Jack decided:

- Targets: one draw of 1,000,000 TrEMBL sequences, in three forms: original, reversed, and each sequence shuffled on its own.
- The draw is sampled by length to cover as wide a range as TrEMBL allows: equal counts per doubling length bin, a bin that runs short handing its quota to the rest.
- Queries: all of Pfam.
- nail at its defaults, with the reporting threshold opened so every pair it aligns is reported.
- The figure is the existing one: cell fraction against query length × target length, one overlaid log-density colormap per form.

pid's `parse cells` and its plot move here. The score figure gets a benchmark of its own separately.

notes.author: jackroddy/8a8c213b
notes.text: `benchmarks/cells/scripts/plot.py` draws the three forms with matplotlib's `Blues`, `Reds` and `Greens` colormaps. Jack wants them built from Paul Tol's palette instead, the one every other figure uses. Original takes blue `#0077BB` and reversed takes red `#CC3311`. Tol's vibrant set has no green, so shuffled needs another of its colours. Teal `#009988` is the nearest.
